title: Stable radix sort from the least to the most significant digit
summary: Ten eight-digit integers are stably sorted at each position, from digit 1 (ones) to digit 8 (ten millions). The final order is ascending by the entire number.
context: The input array nums contains ten eight-digit decimal integers, such as student IDs. The table gives all values. Digit index k starts at 1 for the rightmost digit (ones). Digit 2 is the tens place, and so on up to 8, the leftmost digit (ten millions).
description: Read each of the four data columns independently from top to bottom, at array indices 0 through 9: input, after sorting by ones, after sorting by tens, and final output. A row gives the contents of the same position at different times, not the path of one particular integer. All five passes for digits 3 through 7 run even though their intermediate states are omitted.

Each pass uses stable counting sort on the current digit. Equal digits preserve the relative order from the previous pass. For example, 35663510 and 88906420 both have 0 in position 1 (ones) and remain in their original order after that pass. At position 2 (tens), 81883077 and 30524779 both have 7. The first number, with ones digit 7, therefore stays ahead of the second, with ones digit 9.

A more significant digit takes precedence over the order established by less significant digits. Stability preserves that earlier order whenever the more significant digits match. Each pass moves the entire eight-digit integers, keeping the digits within each integer intact.

prose.summary: The four states show the input, the order after ones, the order after tens, and the result after all eight digits. Passes for digits 3 through 7 run but are not individually pictured.

steps.title: Digit sorting has not started
steps.explanation: The ten eight-digit integers are still in input order. Sorting is about to start at the rightmost digit, position 1 (ones).
steps.key_state: Input order, ready to start stable sorting at digit 1 (ones).
steps.announcement: Initial state: ten eight-digit integers in input order, ready to sort by ones.

steps.title: Ones pass complete
steps.explanation: Stable sorting by digit 1 (ones) has moved whole eight-digit integers into order by their ones digits. Both 35663510 and 88906420 end in 0, so the former still precedes the latter.
steps.key_state: Stable sorting by digit 1 (ones) is complete. Numbers with equal ones digits retain their input order.
steps.announcement: Ones pass complete. Both 35663510 and 88906420 end in 0, and 35663510 still comes first.

state_tables.caption: Radix sort, step 2: array after sorting by ones

steps.title: Tens pass complete
steps.explanation: Starting from the ones-sorted array, stable sorting by digit 2 (tens) puts the last two digits together in ascending order. Both 81883077 (ones digit 7) and 30524779 (ones digit 9) have tens digit 7, so 81883077 still comes first. Digits 3 through 8 remain.
steps.key_state: Stable sorting by digit 2 (tens) is complete. The lowest two digits together are in ascending order.
steps.announcement: Tens pass complete. The last two digits together are sorted; among numbers with tens digit 7, 81883077 still precedes 30524779.

state_tables.caption: Radix sort, step 3: array after sorting by tens

steps.title: All eight digit passes complete
steps.explanation: After the omitted stable passes for digits 3 through 7, the stable pass for digit 8 (ten millions) finishes. The ten eight-digit integers are now in ascending order by their full value.
steps.key_state: Digits 1 through 8 are complete. Output the array in ascending order.
steps.announcement: Finish the stable passes for digits 3 through 7 and then the highest digit, 8, to produce the full sorted array.
